paths.title: Tenant argument reaches another tenant's report store
paths.asset: Confidential reports belonging to other tenants
paths.precondition: The attacker has any valid account and knows another tenant identifier.
steps: app/tenant.py:5 trusts the tenant argument without comparing the session tenant.
app/reports.py:10 reads the selected tenant's report.
mitigations: Bind report lookup to the authenticated session tenant.
paths.analysis: Every link is reachable; no code compares the requested tenant with the caller's session.
paths.remediation: Derive the tenant from the authenticated session and reject cross-tenant requests.
paths.remediation_risks: Legitimate administrative impersonation needs an explicit separately authorized flow.
paths.validation: Add a test proving one tenant cannot read another tenant's report.

paths.title: Report path components escape the report root
paths.asset: Local text files readable by the service process
paths.precondition: The attacker controls the report path and knows a readable target pathname.
steps: app/routes.py:8 accepts an untrusted report path.
app/tenant.py:6 returns another untrusted path component without validation.
app/reports.py:9 joins the components without containment checks and app/reports.py:10 reads the result.
evidence: REPORT_ROOT / tenant / report_name has no absolute-path, parent-directory, or resolved-containment check.
paths.impact: Read service-accessible text outside the intended report directory.
mitigations: UTF-8 decoding and filesystem permissions limit eligible targets but do not enforce containment.
capabilities_required: A low-privilege account and a known target path
capabilities_gained: Read local files outside the report root
paths.analysis: Both path components reach file reading without any containment defense.
paths.remediation: Resolve the authorized tenant root and candidate, then reject absolute paths, traversal, and every target outside that root.
paths.remediation_risks: Canonicalization must preserve valid report names and avoid symlink and time-of-check/time-of-use escapes.
paths.validation: Reject controlled absolute and parent-directory fixtures outside the authorized root while retaining legitimate report reads.

paths.title: Absolute special-file path drives unbounded reads
paths.persona: Unauthenticated caller of the public report route
paths.asset: Availability of report workers and the host process
paths.precondition: The attacker controls the report path and can select a readable endless or very large input on a typical POSIX deployment.
steps: app/routes.py:8 accepts an absolute special-file path.
app/reports.py:9 discards prior path components when joining the absolute input.
app/reports.py:10 reads until EOF without a byte limit, regular-file check, timeout, or cancellation.
evidence: path.read_text(encoding='utf-8') accumulates the entire input, while an endless character device has no EOF.
paths.impact: Occupy a worker and grow process memory until report service or host capacity is exhausted.
mitigations: Filesystem permissions and external resource limits may constrain targets and blast radius but are not in-scope controls.
capabilities_required: Control of the report path and a readable endless or large input
capabilities_gained: Drive unbounded blocking reads and memory consumption
paths.analysis: The absolute-path primitive reaches an unbounded synchronous read with a concrete endless-input deployment precondition.
paths.defense: No regular-file restriction, byte bound, timeout, or cancellation exists in scope.
paths.remediation: Allow only authorized regular files and enforce a bounded read with request deadlines and memory limits as defense in depth.
paths.remediation_risks: Limits must preserve legitimate report sizes and avoid truncating valid responses silently.
paths.validation: Reject special files and enforce clean failure on controlled oversized inputs while preserving ordinary bounded reports.
